column2: Adverbs of something reached at last (ついに, とうとう), after which a やった is a success (ついにやった 드디어 해냈다).
Degree adverbs that may stand between the て form and the word of feeling (来てくれて本当に 嬉しい).
Starts of the words of doing something against one's will (無理やり, 強制的に, 強制労働), which already say the 억지로 of a causative-passive in their clause.
Adverbs of gradual change before a ている of なる, which make it a progression (次第になっている, どんどんなっている).
Adverbs of manner before a kana いく of things going well (上手くいった 잘 되었다), not before いう.
Words of frequency before a past verb with ものだ, which make it what one used to do (昔は遊んだものだ 옛날에는 놀곤 했다).
Adverbs of habit and frequency: a ますか question with one of them asks what someone usually does, not an offer (毎日勉強しますか 매일 공부합니까).
Adverbs that need a negative after them (二度と, 決して, 到底): with an affirmative verb in a quotation before a sentence-final 思うな the な is the negative, a prohibition (二度と会えると思うな 두 번 다시 만날 수 있다고 생각하지 마).
Adverbs of frequency, degree and judgement before which a present verb with ね is what the speaker sees, not a promise (よく食べるね 잘 먹네, なかなかやるね).
The forms of ある after the で of である (であり, である, であった, であれば, であろう).
The spellings of the stem of もらう that follow a て form as the benefactive (見せてもらう, 見せて貰う).
Starts of the auxiliaries of supposition that take the predicate before a pause (行く……かも, 来る……だろう).
Kana stems of the auxiliary verbs that follow a て form: いく, みる, くる, しまう.
Starts of the auxiliaries that follow a て form (ている, てしまう, てほしい, ていただく).
Words that end in んな and are no prohibition spelled with ん (ごめんな is no ごめるな).
What follows だけ and no verb stem (いただけだ, いただけで, いただけじゃ, いただけに, いただけなんです).

The dictionary words of the Kansai ちゃう that is じゃない after a noun (マザコンちゃうわ 마더 콤플렉스 아니거든); after a verb the same kana are the contracted てしまう (やっちゃうね), and constraint chau-after-verb drops the word there.
The copula forms after which そ starting a clause is そう said short (そだね, そであった, そでもない, そじゃない).
The copula forms after a clause-initial そ that make it そう only where the sentence ends after them (あ、そだ。).
The copula forms of copula.short-so-final that also need the start of a sentence, not a comma, before そ (そだった。; not 大きく、そだった, 育った).
What follows the ん that a noun before it says for の (頭ん中 頭の中, 先生んとこ 先生のとこ).
Starts of the text after a ん that says the る of a verb's dictionary form, the な of a prohibition with what may follow it (見んなよ 見るなよ, 来んなって).
The same before no kana, kanji or letter (こっち見んな 見るな, 邪魔すんな); not ごめんな or こんな, words that span the ん.
Starts of the text after a ん that says the ら of a godan verb's negative stem, the られ of a potential or the れ that ends an ichidan stem (分かんない 分からない, 信じらんない 信じられない, してくんない してくれない).
The same with ねえ for ない, which is written as ない (変わんねえ 変わらない, やってらんねえ やってられない).
Starts of the text after a ん that is the negative ない after an ichidan or potential stem (負けんぞ 負けないぞ, 許せんから 許せないから, 食べんか 食べないか).
Starts of contraction.n-negative after which the ん is no such ない (食べんかった, the past said with ん).
The kana after which a verb stem of one kana starts a contracted form (気にすんな, してくんない, かもしんない, 俺がやっから); elsewhere a lone kana is no stem.
Starts of the text after a っ that says the る of a verb's dictionary form (やっから やるから, すっから するから).
Starts of the text after the と or ど that a て form says for its て or で and the お of おる (聞いとる 聞いておる, 読んどった 読んでおった, 聞いとらん 聞いておらん).
Starts of the text after a て form that are the いく after it contracted, in a form (連れてった, 置いてかないで, 持ってかれた, 持ってってくれ, 食べてってね, 持ってけよ).
The forms of the potential of くる without its ら that follow a て form (帰ってこれた, ついてこれる, 戻ってこれました); not これなら or これまで, where これ is the pronoun.
Starts of the text after a て form that are the いる or いらっしゃる after it with its い dropped (見てる, 見てた, 見てて, 見てれば, 見てよう, 見てろ, 見てちゃ, 待ってられない, ついてらっしゃい).
The greeting said with the い of いらっしゃい dropped, which stays as said, drawn out too (いってらっしゃーい 잘 다녀와).
Marks after a predicate that end its sentence, where an end or pattern row of a contraction applies (見てたぜ！); not a comma or an emoticon (忘れてたぜ(^_^)).

Starts of the text after a て form whose past た of a contracted いる stays as said and is read by the word stage on the past of いる (見てたか 보고 있었는지, 見てたやつ 보던 녀석, 考えてたん・・・ 생각하고 있었던), where the full form does not yet read as well. Not after ちゃう.
Kana after the past た of a contracted いる with which its predicate ends: a copula said after it or its vowel drawn out (忘れてたですわ, 待ってたああ), not a word it describes (見てたところ).
The て forms of ちゃう and ちまう after the stem of a て form (寝ちゃって, 読んじゃって, 寝ちまって), a て form before the いる of contraction.te-iru (寝ちゃってた).
Starts of the text after a て form said た or だ that are the あげる after it with its あ dropped (作ったげる, 見せたげよう, 読んだげます).
Starts of the text after a て form said た or だ that are the やる after it with its や dropped (やったるぜ, 調整したるから, やったります).
The same before no kana, kanji or letter (やったる！); not before a particle or a noun, where たる is the attributive (取り出したるは, 秘めたる力).
Starts of the text after a て form that are the contracted いく before a mark or the end when the dictionary holds the verb with ていく (連れてって, 持ってけ); otherwise the quoting って (やめてって).
Starts of the text after a て form that are the contracted いく when the dictionary holds the verb with ていく (連れてってよ); otherwise the quoting って (やめてってよ).
The ってね after the て forms that ask someone to stop or wait, which no one does on the way: it quotes the request, never a contracted いく (やめてってね 그만두라고, 待ってってね 기다리라고).
Starts of the text after a て form that are no contracted いく: the quoting ったら (待ってったら).
Starts of the text after the kanji stem of a godan verb in う that say its past or て form with う for っ (言うた, 思うて).
Starts of the text of contraction.u-onbin that go on as another word (救うため, 戦うたび, 歌うたい).
Counters after which an Arabic 1 in an idiom of counting is the bare native 하나, as the kanji one reads (1つ残らず 하나 남김없이).

Counters of things and actions that もう before a number adds one or more of (もう一匹 한 마리 더, もう１錠 1정 더); no counter of a time, an age, a floor or an order, after which もう is the time reached (もう三年 벌써 3년).
Short names of units that a kanji number before them numbers, read as digits (二水戦 2수전, 一航戦 1항전, 三一駆 31구, 四戦隊 4전대); kanji digits written on without 十 before one read by place value.
Ends of a word that join its clause to the next one (行って, 行けば, 行くけど, 行くので).

Ends of a predicate that close what was said or thought, after which a separate と quotes it (熱いんじゃないかなぁと想像して, 何があったんだと心配そうに, 見たいんだと): sentence particles, the explanatory んだ, たい, the past and a reason or condition said as a wish (から, ば); not だろう or ます, whose と is also a concession or a condition (だろうとなんだろうと, いただけますと).
Starts of an ending or of the next word that make a verb before them negative (いけない, いけません, いけず).
Starts of ending.negative-start after which the verb is not negated: the の said ん before じゃ (できんじゃん できるじゃん, 出せんじゃない).

Starts of ending rows written with 지 않 that negate no verb stem before them: questions that expect a yes (じゃないか, ではありませんか, んじゃないの), the negation of a copula, an adjective or an auxiliary in the ending (でない, くありません, いない, おらず, いただかない, きれず), guesses quoted (かと, しまいかと) and choices (と 1지 않든지).
Ends of the clause before a final な that keep the な as it is, not the exclamation なあ the normalizer makes of な after a clause in が (お前が言うな, 勝てると思うな, 先生ですな).
Forms after られ that make the られ of a transitive or listed verb the passive (られている, られてる, られており, られてた, and ちゃう, which happens to one: 忘れられちゃった).
Forms after られ that make it the potential: negative, conditional, volitional and the polite non-past (られない, られれば, られよう, られます).
Sulky tags after a sentence particle drawn out with its ー (分かりましたよーだ, 知らないもんねーっだ): what follows the ー is tone, not a copula, and is dropped.
The kana after which よーだ of ending.taunt is ようだ spelled long, not a sulky tag (夢のよーだ, 静かなよーだ).

Conditions and concessions after (ら)れ: when the main clause is a trouble of stem.adverse-outcome the (ら)れ is the passive (見られたら困る), and a word of word.ability-scope before one makes no potential (誰だってそう言われたら).
Forms of wanting after (ら)れ, which only the passive takes (褒められたい, 見られたくない).
Polite forms after (ら)れ; in a question with no subject they ask the listener, whose act the (ら)れ honours (何を読まれているんですか 무엇을 읽고 계십니까).
Starts of the polite ます that only a verb form takes, before which a longer word that spells the continuative or the potential stem of a verb is that verb (喜びます, 急ぎます, 頑張れます).
What follows the ん of a contracted いる after a particle (にいんの, でいんだ).
What follows the ん of a contracted ている (てんじゃ, てんだろ).
What follows いた as an adjective ending (見ていたい) or as 致す and 頂く (でいたします, ていただく).
What follows a count of things to say how they are shared or measured: ずつ, 分 and the times sign (二面ずつ 두 면씩, 四面分 네 면분, 四面×四面 네 면×네 면).
The particles and predicates after which a katakana spelling of an adjective reads as the word (ウルサイって, スゴイじゃ).
The sentence-final particles after which a katakana spelling of an i-adjective reads as one (ウルサイぞ).
Endings after which the hiragana spelling of a katakana run that no katakana word reads is an i-adjective stem (クサい, オモシロかった).

What a katakana adverb read in hiragana takes after it as part of its key (シッカリと, ロクに), and the particles and verb starts before which a katakana mimetic said twice reads as an adverb (ジワジワと, ドロドロに, イロイロやる).
What may follow a katakana noun: particles, the copula and honorifics (イカなんて, イカを).
The particles and predicates after which a katakana spelling of a pronoun or noun reads as the word (アレは, ソレだ); アレ before ？ is the interjection.
What else follows a katakana spelling of a verb (コロスんだ, コロスから).
Starts of an item that is not a verb or adjective on its own: a copula or particle at its start (で, じゃ, っ).
What follows a noun and never a verb stem: copulas, particles, ある (わけだ, わけが, わけあって), and what also follows the stem of a verb in its own use (わけ、, わけない 分けない, わけは).
The と that quotes the katakana run before it, which leaves the run a sound (メキメキという, ゴロゴロと言う).
What follows a kana verb stem in its own use as well as a noun: the negative, は, も and に (わけない 分けない, わけは).
The starts of the verb forms after the て of a t-row godan imperative that a phrase row holds (待てない, 待てって, 待てば, 待てる, 待てた), after which the row gives way to the verb.
What may follow a verbal noun that goes on past a counter, so that the number counts its action (1回復した, 1回復を): the forms of する and できる and particles.
First characters of the number after the 分の of a fraction (十分の一 10분의 1, 三分の二, 何分の一).
What follows the denominator of a fraction written with a kanji number (十分の一 10분의 1).
Familiar name suffixes of the dictionary that are words only after a name or a noun of persons or animals (先生たん, 小林っち, 猫たん; not たまごっち, 顔合わせたんだ, 母たんこぶ).
Honorifics after which a name spelled like a number is the name, not the number (九十九さん).
Honorifics after a name that the constraint rules find at the start of the text after it (さん, 先生, ちゃん).
The familiar honorifics of honorific.constraint (くん, ちゃん), a subset of it, which the rules about familiar address look for alone.
Greetings that end like an honoured person in 様 or さま and call no one (お疲れさま、また明日 수고했어, 내일 보자).
Honorifics that a name may draw out before their final ん, with ー, ～ or the vowel of the kana before it (圭ちゃ～ん, 田中さぁあん, アルくぅん).
Honorifics without a final ん that a speaker draws out after themselves before a pause (姫さまぁ 공주님~, 様ーっ), marked as the drawn honorifics are.

Words that end in the kana of a drawn-out honorific but hold none (かいさん 해산), whose drawl stays a lengthening (かいさーん 해산~), pronouns that end in 様 or さま (貴様ぁ, 俺様ぁ, きさまぁ), and words that end in 様 and name no one (有様ぁ, 同様あ).
Drawn-out honorifics that a greeting or an interjection takes as a familiar tag: the phrase keeps its reading and the drawl (おはようちゃーん 좋은 아침~, お待たせちゃーん 기다렸지~).

Apologies, greetings and replies said with a drawn-out honorific of honorific.phrase-tag as a familiar tag like a greeting, WORD or WORD=CASUAL with the casual spelling the tag gives the word (ごめんちゃーん 미안~, よろしく=よろしくね: よろしくちゃーん 잘 부탁해~).
Kanji honorifics of honorific.drawn-after with their kana reading, KANJI=KANA, whose last vowel the speaker draws them out with (様=さま: 姫様ぁ 공주님~).
Titles and suffixes of a person the speaker honours (陛下, 王子, 先生, シンシア様), matched at the end of a word.
Honorifics found at the start of the kana after a name, the longest winning (さくらちゃん, みなみ先生).
Honorifics that fuse with a kanji name into one run (市松殿).
The katakana honorifics a katakana name may end in (ヨウタサン).
Person suffixes that follow a name (さん, 様, 先生), with their drawn-out spellings (さぁん, ちゃーん); a label or run that ends in one is the name before it.
The honorifics that make the hiragana before them a nickname (みっちゃん, けんくん); the last one that starts the text wins.
The titles that show a name to be a person when they follow it (霧島さん, 千歳お姉, 加賀改二).
Honorifics that the rules left untranslated, which leave the spacing to the word after them (魔王ちゃんの 마왕의).
Honorifics read 씨 or 군 that are written apart from the noun before them (田中さん 다나카 씨).
Ship types and ranks a ship's name follows (駆逐艦時雨, 軽巡「川内」, 戦艦、大和): the word after one is the ship's name (names::NameCues).
Titles that a katakana name follows written right after them (聖女アヤメ, 勇者アレン).
Words after a name that make it a name: a sister's title, a remodel number (時雨姉さん, 霞改二).
Words after a ship's name of two kanji or more that make it the name of its class (陽炎型, 睦月型); after a name they read 급 (cx:name-class).
Phrases of naming after a name (アヤメと名乗った, 村雨という名の, まるゆと申します).
What follows 、 after a speaker's own name at the start of an utterance: a call to action (時雨、出撃するよ, 狭霧、参ります).
The copulas and よ that make a self-introduction of a name before the end of the sentence (睦月です。, 陽炎よ。, まるゆでち！).
Starts of the text after a word whose common sense is weather, the sky or the sea, that keep that sense though a cue names the word (時雨が降る, 雷が落ちた, 陽炎が立つ, 潮が満ちる).
ASCII digits and letters: a kanji right after one in its token follows a number or a unit (10cm砲).
Small kana and marks that draw out the kana before them (マルマルぅ, くぅん, ちゃーん).
Kana that start the ending of an end row but no word, so that such an ending is no piece of a katakana run read as words (っしゅ of トリッシュ).
The kin, pet and other words before ちゃん the dictionary lacks in hiragana, which are no nickname (にいちゃん, わんちゃん, いっちゃん 一番).
The second and fourth kana of a four-kana katakana run, in hiragana, that make it the shape of a native adverb (シッカリ, ヒンヤリ).
Final syllables of Korean adjective stems: their 지 않다 is the negative of an adjective (기분이 좋지 않다, 좋지 않은), not of a verb (않는다, 않는).
Korean nouns of what one undergoes whose causative-passive (させられる after the Japanese noun) is the noun with 당하다 (해고당하다, 퇴학당하다), not the act one is made to do.
Korean nouns of 하다 whose passive is the noun with 받다 (사과받다); nouns of neither this set nor ko-noun.passive-danghada take 되다 (고용되다).
Korean nouns of 하다 whose passive is the noun with 당하다 (무시당하다).
Korean nouns of 하다 whose passive keeps 어지다 (말하다 말해지다, 의지하다).
Korean laughs the sound stage writes (아하하, 후후), after which おかしい is funny, not strange (あはは、おかしい 아하하, 웃겨).
Ends of Korean present verbs that state, not plan, and so are written plainly in 해체 (모른다 몰라, 생각한다 생각해, 마음에 든다 마음에 들어).
Ends of Korean lemmas that read a passive or potential (쓰여지다, 결정되다, 읽히다, 올 수 있다), which the respectful form replaces; a verb of its own (生まれ 태어나다) keeps its Korean.
Times signs: a count after one counts too (四面×四面 네 면×네 면).

Korean verbs of holding, wearing, touching, posture and knowing, whose 고 있던 is the state the action left (抱えていた子供 안고 있던 아이, 忘れていた 잊고 있던); 던 would read as a habit. A phrase that ends in one counts too (이를 악물다).
Korean verbs that take the person they act on as their object, (을)를: after a verb of verb.ni-partner read so, the person's に is (을)를 (私に勝てる 나를 이길 수 있다, 彼に会った 그를 만났다).

Korean passive verbs whose patient is their subject and never an object (불리다, 끊기다): the を object of a passive read with one, or with 어지다 or 되다, is its subject (名前を呼ばれた 이름이 불렸다); a passive that takes the part or the thing one loses as its object (발을 밟히다, 지갑을 빼앗기다) is not one.
Korean verbs of actions done one after the other (먹다, 씻다, 자다), whose て reads 고.
Last syllables of Korean that ends an utterance, by which a set phrase reads as something said (힘내라, 고마워, 수고하셨습니다).
The Korean that the sound stage writes only for interjections of noticing (あっ 앗), before which a そうだ standing alone recalls something; not 음, which it writes for うむ and んー too.
Starts of the Korean of 하다 and 되다 in their forms (하, 한, 했, 되, 된, 돼, and $Kz@, 하다 in a word of the adjective class), which show that a する joins its verbal noun.
The ending of an adjective that the past adnominal 있던 of a progressive becomes when the simple aspect drops it (困ってたところ 곤란했던 곳).
The Korean of the いる after a て form whose い is dropped before an ending row of the past (見てたぞ 보고 있었어), ending in the marker family that the ending after it conjugates.
The Korean of the ちゃう in its て form before a いる whose い is dropped (寝ちゃってたんだ 자 버린 거야), ending in the marker family that the ending after it conjugates.
The Korean endings of a name after which a following honorific is written as nothing (님, 씨, 선배).
Marks right after an offer of あげる outside brackets that make it a line of dialogue, as a final particle does (見せてあげる！ 보여 줄게!, 見せてあげるっ！).
Latin letters a run of which laughs after Korean in the output (없어ｗｗ 없어ㅋㅋ).
The Korean written for each laughing letter of mark.laughter.
The Korean written in the brackets of a bracketed run of mark.laughter ((w) (웃음)), as for (笑).
Marks after which a run of mark.laughter still laughs (진짜야!ｗ).
Closing brackets, before which no space follows a sentence end (정말? 」 정말?」, 없습니다. 』 없습니다.』) and after which the speech of a quote does not go on.
Exclamation marks: a question with one after it is a surprised remark, not an offer (待ち伏せますか！).
Answers a prompt on a screen lists after its question, anywhere in the text that follows it (乗りますか？乗るやめる, やりますか？やるやらない).
What follows the question mark of a prompt shown on a screen: a quoting と, a closing 》 and the answers (開始しますか？という, 取得しますか？》, はい／いいえ, （はい／いいえ）).
Ellipses and dashes (also two katakana or Latin middle dots) after which a word restarts what was being said (私が…私が).
Commas, before which an utterance goes on (また明日、学校で).
Question marks, after which a row read only where the utterance ends asks instead (また明日？ 또 내일?).
The bare endings of the last copy of an adjective or adjectival noun said again as a predicate (痛い痛い, 嫌だ嫌だ).
The Korean endings of that last copy that the copies may recast: the plain 1다 and the exclamative 6.
Adjectives that said twice with nothing after them are a grumble, written as a 1다 and 6 pair (寒い寒い 춥다 추워), where other adjectives said again are a cry in 6 (痛い痛い 아파 아파).
Verbal nouns of moving to a post or a place whose する in the て form before 来る says the arrival (転属してきている 전속해 와 있다, 帰国してきている 귀국해 와 있다).
Nouns of what keeps coming, whose 来ている comes on rather than has arrived (いい風きてる 좋은 바람 오고 있어, 波が来ている 파도가 오고 있다).
Kinship words that たん and っち after them belong to, as ちゃん does (お兄ちゃんたん 오빠, 妹たん 여동생).
Words without conjugation that are a predicate in Korean (だめ 안돼): said again and clipped with っ, the last copy closes with ㅅ like an adjective (だめだめっ 안돼 안됏).
Korean words written joined to a form of 되다 right after them (안 돼 안돼, 안 된다 안된다).
Korean auxiliary verbs, by their selected Korean, written joined to the 아/어 form before them when the Japanese entry is an auxiliary (gram Ds) (먹어 버렸다 먹어버렸다).
Marks right after the last copy of an adjective of adjective.grumble said twice that make the copies a cry (寒い寒いっ, 寒い寒い！, 寒い寒いー, 寒い寒い……, 寒い寒い♪).
The clipping small tsu after a cry (痛い痛いっ 아파 아파앗).
Vowel kana that draw out the word before them into an exclamation (燃えるねぇ, 言うねェ).
Marks that open a thought, which an adjective drawn out in it does not make a cry (（む、難しい〜〜） 어렵다~~).
Marks that close what mark.thought-open opens.
Marks that stretch an い-adjective at the end of its phrase into a cry (暑いー！ 더워~!, 痛い～ 아파~).
Marks that draw out the word before them: after a final な of 思う they make it the speaker's opinion (思うなぁ, 思うなー).
Long marks that draw out a kana inside a word: a copy of a word drawn out with them is the same word (すごい|すごーい).
Marks of a pause in speech: an ellipsis or a dash (……と、, そう――と).
Marks that end a sentence: a line in て with one of them before is speech, not a verse line (…よ？私に任せて).
Marks of a main clause that is a supposition, hearsay, a degree or a habit rather than an event that followed (しまいそうだった, 崩すほど重かった, 使えるらしく, という欠点).
Marks that end the sentence a (ら)れ verb asks in (何を読まれているんですか？).
Ends of a question after a (ら)れ verb, the last kana of its sentence or the mark after it (確認されますか, 読まれているんですか？).
Nouns that name a quality: the の before an adjective after them is the subject (香りの良い, 面倒見のいい).

Ends of the nouns of a realm, a setting, a group or an event in which something holds or is done: でも after one is 에서도, in it too (王都でも指折り 왕도에서도 손꼽히는, 作戦でも働いた 작전에서도 일했다), not before する, a verb of verb.example-object, どう or a word of permission.
Starts of the nouns that need a modifier, the auxiliaries and the adverbial particles that still take the predicate before a pause (行く……ことにした, 来る……まで).
Japanese nouns of declarations and verdicts, whose する and だ keep 다 (破棄する 파기한다).
Nouns after a verb that name the clause rather than a thing in it (していたの, していたこと, していたようだ, 迎えられたこと).
Verbal nouns of a change that befalls someone or something (中断, 孤立, 停止), whose causative-passive is that change done to one, 되다 (思考を中断させられた 사고가 중단되었다), not an act one is made to do.
Starts of the nouns that an attributive before an ellipsis or a dash still modifies (行く……ことにした).
Ends of nouns of events that are no verbal noun, before which であった after a place is what happened there (海外であった事件 해외에서 있던 사건).
Nouns of angle or temperature earlier in the sentence that make 度 one (角度は四十五度, 体温が三十八度).
Verbal nouns and mimetic words of a feeling that comes over one, whose する is no act one plans (安心する, ドキドキする): with ますね they are what the speaker feels, not a promise.
Nouns of the people a shop or a host speaks to or of: after ご, a verbal noun and の they are the ones who did it (ご予約のお客様 예약하신 손님, ご参加の皆様 참가하신 여러분).
Ends of verbal nouns of what the honored person goes on doing, read in 하시는 rather than 하신 before noun.honored-person (ご利用のお客様 이용하시는 손님, ご希望の方 희망하시는 분).
Nouns whose inside is filled, or that one is in as a medium, a time or a state, not a container: 中 after them and の is 속 (물속, 기억 속, 밤 속, 정적 속).
Speaker labels that name a group, a voice or a role, not a person (みんな, 声, アナウンス, 店員).
Nouns that make an adverb of manner with に, after which いう is to say, not to go (一括りにいっても 말해도, 端的にいえば 말하면).
Ends of the nouns of prices, rates and markets: as the subject of 反発 they rebound, 반등 (株価が反発した 주가가 반등했다).
Ends of the nouns before に that tell a point in time or what else, not the place or state one goes back to (三時に戻る 3시에 돌아오다, 一時間後に戻る, それ以外に戻る理由).
Kanji compounds before する that tell a time, a frequency or an amount, and stay an adverb apart from the verb (全部します 전부 합니다).
Nouns before になっている that read as an ongoing state (話題になっている 화제가 되고 있다).
Nouns of experience and practice that 積む piles up rather than loads, before which 一杯 and いっぱい read 많이 (経験もいっぱい積んだ 경험도 많이 쌓았다); written as words of a senses.tsv trigger.
Place and time nouns that start a word after a の the rules left untranslated (가게 안, 침대 아래, 아이 때).
The nouns that a quotation in って modifies (って奴 라는 녀석).
Verbal nouns of asking, wishing, answering and ordering whose する takes what is asked or wished with って (静かにってお願いした 조용히라고 부탁했다, 場所って希望した 장소라고 희망했다).
Nouns in 国 that take the 国 of a country or province name before them (美濃国境 미노 국경, 日本国内 일본 국내); 国中, 国府 and 国主 keep the name with its 国.
The modern countries of noun.realm-name, which noun.realm-province-compound does not split (日本国人).
Names of countries and old provinces that are written with 国 (日本国, 越中国, 美濃国).
Nouns in 国 that take the 国 of an old province name before them, not of a modern country (出羽国人 데와 고쿠진).
Verbal nouns whose されている is a state (舗装されている).

Ends of the nouns of here, of a ship's home port and of one's right mind (正気): 戻る to them, or in a sentence that names here after it, comes back, 돌아오다 after (으)로 (こっちに戻る 여기로 돌아오다, 母港に戻る 모항으로 돌아오다, 正気に戻る 제정신으로 돌아오다, 車に戻ったんだ、ここも 차로 돌아왔어).
Person nouns beyond noun.role (あの人, 誰か, お母さん, あいつ): a が, は or も after one of them before an offer of あげる names another giver (あの人が作ってあげる！ 그 사람이 만들어 준다!).
Words of kinship, address, rank and role: a label or name candidate that is one is a role, not a name (父, 店長, 勇者, マスター).
Ends of the nouns of a fleet, a unit or a team that acts as one: で after one before a verb of verb.unit-operation is the group that does it, (으)로 (艦隊で出撃する 함대로 출격한다), not the scope (艦隊で一番 함대에서 제일).
Ends of the words of a span or a unit before which ごと shares out, 마다 (数時間ごと 몇 시간마다, 三ページごと), not 째.
Ends of the nouns before which ごと is 事, a matter (お願いごと, 面倒ごと, 争いごと), not the whole of a thing taken with it, 째.
Nouns of position and situation, after which から and the particle of place read 에서 (後ろから, 現場で).
Verbal nouns whose Korean takes 받다 as one verb (소개받다, 지급받다): right before してもらう they keep 받다 with the giver in 에게 (先生に紹介してもらった 선생님에게 소개받았다).
Nouns of noun.scene that also name a thing one uses: before a verb of verb.means-de their で is the means (夢で取り繕う 꿈으로 꾸미다, 夢で終わる 꿈으로 끝나다).
Vehicles: their で is the means only before a verb of verb.vehicle-travel, and elsewhere the place where it happens (電車で行く 전철로 가다, 電車で足を踏まれた 전철에서 발을 밟혔다).
Nouns of what is done to someone (こと, 何): a bare される right after one, or after its を, is the passive of する, 당하다 (どんなことされたの 어떤 일을 당했어), unless GRM-10 reads it respectful.
Ends of the words of time before から, which then reads 부터 (三時から, 昔から, 少し前から).
Words that start with an honorific: after a name they are the title (殿下, 様子).
Particles after which, or before which after a kanji or katakana, a single Latin letter of mark.laughter is a word, not laughter (変数wの値, のwキー).
Numerals that start a number with its counter in one word (一匹, 二人, 数本, 1回).

Numerals of numeral.lead that start a count of more than one (10 to 19 start the numbers of two or more digits that begin with 1), after which もう before a past verb is the count reached (もう二人来た 벌써 두 사람 왔다).
Particles that may follow a name where a verb or adjective stem would take its inflection.
Particles after which a word reads as a predicate, not as an utterance of its own (そんなのゴメンよ 싫어).
The case particles after which a verb stem in kana goes on (二つにわけ、, パンをわけない).
Particles after ではない or ではなかった that make a contrast that goes on (大した傷ではないが), which keeps the topic particle.
Particles that may stand between 度 and a word of word.do-angle.
Particles that after a person make the (ら)れ of their clause the potential (子供でも着られる).
Starts of the word after 程 or ほど that make it a degree (それほどの, 程まで).
Particles that, after the first character of an item, make a phrase that starts with a noun.
Particles that close a quotation; a に right before one is inside it and no agent of a (ら)れ verb after it (次の王になんて言われたら).
Particles and final particles after the て of 見る before which it stays the 어 of a て form, not the 고 of an action done first (見てはいけない, 見てよ).
Case particles that, between two kanji or katakana of a name-layer key, make the key a phrase that reads as a title only standing apart (星に願いを, 世界を救う).
Particles of an agent besides に before a (ら)れ verb (先生によって選ばれた).
Particles of a subject, a topic, an experiencer or a source before a (ら)れ verb, after which a polite question asks about that one, not the listener.
The particles a question word may run on with in one word (何を, 誰の, どこへ, いつから).
The marks that may stand between two copies of a word said again (待って、待って).
The first-person pronouns 私, わたくし, あたし, 僕 and 俺 in kanji, hiragana and katakana; a katakana one beside one in another spelling in its sentence is a second self (ワタシと私).
First-person pronouns whose genitive takes the short form (나의 내, 저의 제).
Pronouns and nouns that end in hiragana, after which a word reads as following a noun (これ, みんな, 予定通り).
First-person pronouns read as the humble 저 or 저희 in polite speech (私はそう思います 저는 그렇게 생각합니다).
Second-person pronouns of rough or scornful speech, alone and plural (お前, 貴様, てめえ, あんた): the subject of a quotation before a sentence-final 思うな, which then forbids (お前が勝てると思うな 네가 이길 수 있다고 생각하지 마).
Second-person pronouns whose genitive takes the short form (너의 네).
Words by which the speaker names himself or herself, alone or with others, as the subject of a promise (私が行くね 내가 갈게).
Second-person pronouns, alone and plural, by which the speaker names the listener (あなた, 君, お前, 貴公ら, そなた): a recipient in に of one of them is the one spoken to.
The pronouns and words after which わ is the topic は spelled as it sounds (こっちわ, お前わ).
Question words before a copula だ that ends a quote or stands before 、 (何だ, 誰だ).
Question words that make a sentence-final だろう a question (何だろう 뭘까, どっちだろう 어느 쪽일까).
Starts of words that begin like a question word but are none (何か, どうせ, いつも).
Starts of what follows a question word that make it an indefinite, which asks nothing (どこにでも, 誰も, 誰でも, 誰であれ).
The quoting form after a sound, read as する before a word in kanji or katakana (カタカタという音 달각달각하는 소리).

Syllables, in katakana, that also stand alone before a separator and a word in kanji (あ、本当 "ah, really", ま、仕方ない "well"; が、 a particle): there they stutter only a word they start (sound.stutter-head) or when said twice.
Syllables of sound.stutter-alone that are the conjunction where they open a line (と、時計を見た, で、電話をかけた), even before a word they start.

Starts of words in kanji after the katakana of the first mora of their reading (マ待, オ俺, ム無理): a syllable that also says something alone (ま、 お、 う、) and a separator before a word it starts are a stutter (ま、待って 기, 기다려). The longest head decides; a head of one kanji is that kanji before kana or a mark (待って, not 待機).
Heads of sound.stutter-head that count only before an ellipsis or a dash: ちょ before a comma is the clipped ちょっと 잠깐 whatever follows (ちょ、直撃 잠깐, 직격; ちょ…直撃 지…직격).
Syllables of sound.stutter-alone that are interjections anywhere, also before an ellipsis or a dash inside an utterance (……あ……先輩) and before a word they start (あ、明日 아, 내일).
Syllables of sound.stutter-alone that alone are particles, so before an ellipsis or a dash they stutter the word after them (……と……大丈夫).
Speech markers inside an utterance that show the speaker to be a woman (ですわ, かしら, あたし).
Speech markers inside an utterance that show the speaker to be a man (俺, だぜ, 兄上).
Marks of old or lordly speech found anywhere in a line (ておる, のじゃ, 拙者).
The classical negative ぬ (ならぬ, 知らぬ), a mark of old speech only before the end of a clause, which 死ぬ is not.
Marks of polite speech found anywhere in a line (です, ます, ください).
Words that hold a mark of speech.polite-grammar and are no polite speech (ますます).
Marks of polite speech found inside a surface, which make the sentence polite (です, ます, ください).
Kanji spellings of a cry, KANJI=KANA, read as the kana where they start an utterance and a drawn-out run follows before a pause (嫌ぁぁぁ いやぁぁぁ, 嫌っ！ いやっ！).
The copula です written in katakana, alone or with a final particle, respelled like spelling.katakana-ending (私デース 私でーす, 秋刀魚デスネー).

Ends of a predicate (a past in た or だ after the kana that a verb conjugates with, a progressive in てる or でる) after which spelling.katakana-copula stays in katakana: the verb and です do not make a sentence (言ったデース, 何してるデース; not あなたデス, まだデス).
Ends of spelling.katakana-copula-kept-after that also count right after a kanji, the stem of a verb (来たデース, 見たデース).
Polite endings of する written in katakana right after a word, before a pause or the end (受信シマシタ), respelled in hiragana with their ー kept (でーす) before lookup.
Endings of spelling.katakana-ending that are respelled only after hiragana, the stem of a verb (行きマース; not 一マス).
Final particles written in katakana, respelled like spelling.katakana-ending but only after hiragana or kanji (楽しいネー, 天気ネ; not Decemberネー).

Old forms of kanji that the Jōyō kanji table gives with their new forms, OLD=NEW: an old form that no dictionary word holds, not even on its own, is written in its new form before lookup, so that both read alike (格好惡い 格好悪い, 隱れる 隠れる; 赤澤 of a name stays).
Spellings of a grammatical word written as its other spelling before lookup, VARIANT=SPELLING, so that both read alike (痛い程に 痛いほどに, 見たとき 見た時).
Kanji variants of spelling.variant also respelled after a kanji or katakana, not only after hiragana (子供程 子供ほど).
The kana after which a kana variant of spelling.variant is respelled: the end of a predicate or of の (あったとき, そのとき; not もっときれい).

Contexts in which a variant of spelling.variant is another word and stays: 位 of rank after の or before が, を (神の位, 位が下げられる), 等 read ら after a pronoun (それ等, あいつ等), the verb 為す or 為る (何を為そう), and 程 after the adnominal な, which the kana rows read as an attached 만큼 (同数な程).
Stems of predicates of trouble or embarrassment, which make the (ら)れ of a condition before them the passive (見られたら困る, 見つめられたら照れる).
Verb stems of the compound particles in て after に, と or を (について 에 대해, によって).
The contractions of て or で with しまう before its own endings (食べちゃうよ, 飲んじゃうよ, 行っちまうよ, 死んじまうよ).
Stems of the honorific godan verbs in る whose polite forms are written with い (くださいます, いらっしゃいませ, ございます).
Stems before い of the predicates of existence, quantity or knowing, whose の before them is the subject (人の少ない).
Second halves of the compound verbs of action on someone (睨み付け, 突きつけ, 投げかけ, 責め立て).
The polite ending and the auxiliaries and suffixes that a verb's continuative runs into as one verb form (余ります, 余り過ぎる, 余り始める, 余りがち, 余りそうだ).
Ends of a speaker label Xの父 that name a relative of the name X (アリスの母).
Ends of a speaker label that make it a role, not a name (サッカー部員, 担当者, 女子生徒).
Person suffixes that follow a surname without being a given name (田中家, 佐藤夫妻).
Plural suffixes that a pronoun runs into as one plural pronoun (私たち, 僕ら, 俺ども).
Title words that may follow a name inside its run (茜たち, 水無月家).
Starts of the する after a verbal noun that make the noun the predicate (回復した, 回復できる).
Starts of the rest of a form of する after its stem し (しない, してる, しちゃう, しよう), not the first kana of まで, なら or たくさん after 今年.
Starts of the する, なさる or できる that join the verbal noun before them (キスしたい 키스하고 싶다, 我慢できない, 購入なさる).
Forms of する written with the marker of 하다 that join the verbal noun before them (即答する 즉답하다).
Starts of Japanese verbs that state (違う, 似る; 高すぎる after an adjective), whatever their Korean.
Dictionary rows of causative-passive verbs (待たされる 기다리게 되다, 食べさせられる 먹다); a person before に is who made it happen.
Stems of verbs of a state that befalls someone (疲れる, 困る, 驚く), whose て form before ちょっと explains and asks for nothing.

Verbs and verbal nouns whose causative-passive is something one goes through, not an act one is made to do (待たされる 기다리게 되다, 驚かされる, 考えさせられる, 心配させられる); dictionary forms for the analysed verbs, the surfaces of dictionary rows in される.
Verbs of time going by (経つ, 過ぎる, する), whose ば or たら after a count with も says once that much has passed (半年も経てば 반년도 지나면).
Verbs of leaving a task to someone (頼む, 任せる), before which 後は is what is left to do.
Verbs of seeing, buying, eating, drinking, making and reading, whose object a noun in でも offers as an example: (이)라도, not the place 에서도 (家でも買うか 집이라도 살까, 本でも読め 책이라도 읽어).
Verbs of moving or changing by some amount, before which ちょっと is how far, not how long (ちょっと離れて 조금 떨어져).

Starts and ends of Japanese verbs of what appears, happens or is felt, which no one does on purpose: with ね they are observed, not promised (始まるね, 思い出すね, 照れるね). Not 出る, which the speaker does (先に出るね 먼저 나갈게).
Starts of words of liking and delight that make a やばい right before or after them praise, 대박 (かわいすぎてやばい, やばい、可愛い).
Starts of verbs of eating and drinking whose polite ますね after an adverb of amount (adverb.amount) remarks on how much the listener eats, not a promise (たくさん食べますね 많이 먹네요; ここで食べますね 먹을게요).
Adverbs of amount that make a polite ますね of eating or drinking a remark (たくさん食べますね, しっかり食べますね).
Adverbs before which a polite ますね comments on what the listener does (急に切り替えますね 갑자기 바꾸네요); with a plain ね they may still promise (急に出かけるね).
Ends of passive stems (言われ, 書かれ, 愛され, 頼まれ, 打たれ, 呼ばれ, 塞がれ, 叱られ), whose ね is what happens to someone, not a promise (また叱られますね 또 꾸중듣네요).
Continuatives of verbs that aim an act at someone or something before かける (話しかける, 微笑みかける, 呼びかける, 追いかける, 振りかける): that かける is part of the verb, not a half-done act.

Continuatives of verbs of a change that befalls the subject rather than an act it does on purpose (なり, 忘れ, 落ち, 転び): with かける after them the change nearly happened or is going on (なりかけた 될 뻔했다, 忘れかけている 잊어 가고 있다).

Verbs of filling, loading and holding, in kanji and kana spellings, and the idioms of tears filling the eyes, before which 一杯 and いっぱい read 가득 (箱にいっぱい詰めた 가득 채워 넣었다, 涙をいっぱいためて); written as words of a senses.tsv trigger.
Verbs of putting in, before which いっぱい or 一杯 right after a container and its に reads 가득 (箱にいっぱい入れた 상자에 가득 넣었다; お砂糖、いっぱい入れて 많이).
Stems of the verbs of staying, waiting and watching, whose て form with a final な tells the listener to keep doing it, ていな (待ってな 기다리고 있어, 見てな 보고 있어), not a reason (思ってな).

Stems of the verbs of an errand one goes to do and comes back from, and the verbal nouns of upkeep before する, whose てまいる is going to do it and coming back (お茶を淹れてまいります 차를 끓여 오겠습니다, 整備してまいります 정비해 오겠습니다); other てまいる go on doing it.
Ends of the verbs whose て form with an object gives the means or manner (道具を使って 도구를 써서); they keep 어.
Ends of the verbs of filling, covering, deceiving and ending that take what they do it with in で (夢で満たす 꿈으로 채우다).
Verbs that take what they write or call something with と (呼ぶ, 名乗る).
Verbs whose own argument is a person in に, the one met, beaten, followed or leaned on (勝つ, 会う, 頼る, 逆らう): their potential does not make that person the one who can (私に勝てる 나를 이길 수 있다, not 내가).
Stems of the verbs of noticing or remembering whose negative takes 못하다 (気づかない 눈치채지 못하다).
Ichidan stems of acts done to someone, whose narrative られた after an object is the passive (決断を命じられた, 罵声を浴びせられた); a conditional of one is passive after its object without a recipient に.
Ichidan stems whose られ reads as the passive whatever their objects (perception and attitude: 恐れられる, 見つめられる).
Ichidan stems whose affirmative られた is mostly the potential (見つけられた, 耐えられた).
Stems that start a verb of saying or thinking, which takes a quotation before it.
Godan stems of permitting, entrusting and taking away, whose subject before the object and (ら)れ is the one acted on (参加を許される, 王位を奪われた).
Stems of the respectful verbs, お〜にな included, whose Korean is the honorific in 시 (仰っている 말씀하고 계신다, お休みになっている 쉬고 계신다).
Stems of the passive verbs whose ている is a state (並べられている, 囲まれている).
Stems of the verbs of moving to a place whose て form before 来る says the arrival, so that its ている is the state of having come (帰ってきている 돌아와 있다, 入ってきている 들어와 있다).
Stems of the verbs whose ている is the state their action left, read without an object (濡れている, 座っている); a compound or phrase that ends in one counts too.
Stems of the result-state verbs whose state reads as the Korean past (亡くなっているから 돌아가셨으니까, 古びている本 오래된 책).
Stems of the verbs of talking and going out with someone that keep the progressive of ている in the plain present and in 지 (付き合っている人 사귀는 사람); a stem ending in 言 or 云 counts too.
Starts of the verbs of speaking after a quotation in って (って言った, って叫ぶ).
Ichidan stems whose られ is a feeling that comes by itself, never the potential (将来が案じられる, 気配が感じられる).
Stems of the verbs of thinking and perceiving whose ている reads as the simple form (見えている 보인다); a stem ending in 思 counts too.
Verbs of giving, handing, telling or asking whose に is the person the act goes to (渡す, あげる, 言う, 頼む).
Verbs of teaching and telling that take what is taught with って (しないようにって教えた, 42って教えた); a と after a noun before one is the partner (友達と教えた), so they are no verb.naming.
Surfaces that start a verb of thinking ahead in the clause.
The よう of manner after a godan continuative with what follows it: a particle, the copula or a mark (疑いようもない 의심할 수도 없다, やりようがある, 品のないなさりよう！). The volitional of an ichidan verb is not read so.
Starts of the verbs and verbal nouns of going, coming, moving and carrying, before which the で of a vehicle (noun.vehicle) is the means (車で行く, 車で迎えに来る, 車で移動, 車で三十分).
Ichidan stems of giving, entrusting, ordering and borrowing, whose に before their (ら)れ names the other party, not who acts (私に弟を任せられた 나에게 남동생을 맡길 수 있었다, 父に車を借りられた).

Verbs of giving, showing, teaching, granting or allowing something to someone, by dictionary form (授ける, 与える, 教える, 見せる, 許す, 叶える, 渡す): their volitional that ends a sentence, with an object, the listener in に or the speaker as subject, and no other recipient and nothing inclusive, is the speaker's will, 주마 (力を授けよう 힘을 내려 주마), not 자.
Starts of the verbs and verbal nouns of a military operation or a joint task that a group in で carries out (出撃, 突撃, 攻略, 達成): the first predicate after the で decides.
Stems of the verbs of writing, whose てある is what stands written (書いてある 써 있다).
Words after a noun that belittle it (ごとき, なんか, 風情): a subject in が after one, in a quotation before a sentence-final 思うな, makes it forbid (お前ごときが勝てると思うな).
Words that make the (ら)れ of their clause the potential: anyone, any time or anywhere, or by oneself (誰でも着られる, 自分で決められる).

Words of the dictionary that a form of いる or いらっしゃる starts (いろ 色, いよう 異様, いたって 至って, いたみ 痛み, いらっしゃい 어서 오세요): right after a て form the text is that いる or いらっしゃる (待っていろよ, 何していようかな, 悔しがっていたみたい, 洗っていらっしゃい).
Words of standing out or doing one's part (活躍, 頑張る, 有名, 最強): a でも right before one after a noun that is no person is 에서도, where it holds (フランス海軍でも活躍した 프랑스 해군에서도 활약했다).
Words that open a concession before the noun in でも, which then stays (이)라도 even in a setting (どんな苦境でも 어떤 곤경이라도, どんな世界でも).
Starts of the words of permission and of being all right, before which a でも is (이)라도 even after a noun of noun.arena (ここでもいい 여기라도 좋아).
Set phrases that end in a closing particle and are an utterance of their own only where the sentence or a clause ends after them (ゴメンな 미안해, not ゴメンなら).
Verbs and nouns of doing something with someone or comparing with something, whose partner takes と (戦う, 結婚, 同じ).
Verbal nouns before する and verb stems of the actions a confirm dialog asks about: a ますか after one offers the act, 까요 (上書きしますか？ 덮어쓰기할까요?, 回復薬を使いますか？ 회복약을 쓸까요?).

Adverbs and nouns that a copula, an adnominal な or a question か after them makes the adjectival noun of the same key (ばっちりです 완벽해요, しっかりですね 확실하네요, アリなのか 괜찮은 건가), not an adverb or a noun before a copula.
Starts of the words after 度 that make it an angle or a temperature: a change of direction, a bend, a turn, a tilt, or a range or step of the value (百八十度変わった, 九十度に曲げる, 三百六十度見渡す, 九十度近く).
What follows 度 when it counts times: 目 (度目 번째), も and ほど (十度も 열 번이나, 五度ほど 다섯 번 정도).
Words that ask to be given what is named before them (もう一枚ください 한 장 더 주세요).
The greetings お帰りなさい and お休みなさい, which are no orders.
Starts of the words after から that keep (으)로부터 (から守る, から逃げる, から身を).
Ends of the words of the humble お〜する and ご〜する that do no favour to another: one rests, waits, accepts, refuses, entrusts, asks, meets or comes along (お休みします 쉴게요, お任せします 맡깁니다), so they take no 드리다.
The spellings of くせに and くせして that blame what goes against the clause or noun before them (知ってるくせに 알면서, 子供のくせに 아이 주제에).
The words after which であ is 出会う (と出会う, ここで会う), not the copula である.

What a word reads with its ending (I) before a dictionary form with ところだった that makes it a narrow miss, 뻔했다: adverbs of a near miss, a slip (一歩間違えば) and relief (危なかった) (危うく落ちるところだった 하마터면 떨어질 뻔했다), not the moment before an act (ちょうど出かけるところだった).

Words before a ますか that make it an offer or a proposal to the listener or to the speaker and the listener (with the first person plural: 私達も, みんなで): 까요 (さて、帰りますか 자, 돌아갈까요, お茶でも飲みますか 차라도 마실까요); an interjection read as a sound span is matched by its Korean (자, 그럼, 좋아).
Words that put the speaker together with others (一緒に, みんなで, 私たち, 我ら): a volitional in their sentence invites, 자 (われらの力を見せよう 우리들의 힘을 보여 주자).

Starts of the words of company, sameness, time or difference before which a と going on from the line before, or after a predicate that could end what was said, is the comitative (と一緒に行こう 와 함께 가자, と同じだ 와 같다, 来たと同時に).
Interjections of noticing or remembering after which a そうだ standing alone recalls something (あ、そうだ 아, 맞다; と、そうだ), not ああ or うん, which agree, nor えっと, which hesitates.
Interjections that may lead a denial or a correction (いや、違う 아니, 아니야; え、違うの？).
Verbs and verbal nouns of supposing or describing that take what they suppose with と (仮定, 見なす).
Starts of the words right after a とは that ask or tell what or who it names, so it defines, (이)란, even after a person (先生とは誰ですか, メイドとは一体何).
Starts of the words of difference, comparison and relationship that take what とは names as their partner, (와)과는 (それとは違う 그것과는 다르다, 答えとは裏腹に, あいつとは仲がいい); without one later in its clause とは defines, (이)란.
Words after これより that make it a comparison, not the start of an action now (これより前, これより先, これよりまし).
Adverbs of degree after which より compares, 보다 (よりずっと, よりもっと).
Starts of the words after which それに is the thing taken up, 거기에, not the conjunction 게다가 (それによって, それに伴って, それに比例して).
Words of thanks, apology and feeling after which a て or 連用 form gives the reason (어서: 와 줘서 기뻐, 도와줘서 살았다).
Words of life, wounds, illness, escape and rescue before which 助かる in the same sentence is surviving, 살아나다 (命が助かった 목숨을 건졌다, 患者は助からない), not help or relief.
